metadata.case_name: KWONG WAN KAU v. YUEN WING HONG

plaintiff.occupation_before: Workman II of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD)

injuries.description: compound fracture of the right distal fibula
source: X ray films revealed compound fracture of the right distal fibula. Emergency operation was performed and the fracture was fixed with metal implants.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the ankle or foot

injuries.description: persistent infection of the wound at the right ankle which took about 10 months to heal
source: By reason of persistent infection, the wound at the Plaintiff’s right ankle took about 10 months to heal up.
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of ankle or foot, unspecified

injuries.description: extensive scarring of the right ankle with resulting gross stiffness
source: He persistently experienced gross stiffness over his right ankle due to extensive scar resulted from the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

manifestations.description: Cannot stand or walk for long hours
Cannot climb, squat or lift heavy things
Weakness on the right lower limb
Difficulty in climbing staircases or walking along slopes

treatments_received: Emergency operation to fix fracture with metal implants
Second operation to remove metal implants (7 October 1999)
Physiotherapy for more than one year
Regular outpatient follow up at the Orthopaedic Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital

losses.description: Cannot stand or walk for long hours; difficulty in climbing staircases or walking along slopes
Weakness on the right lower limb; muscle wasting
Gross stiffness over right ankle due to extensive scarring
